fields.statement: Which intent should Scheduled triggers (01M6W4K) serve? It serves nothing yet. The repo has no .rhiza/policy.toml, so backlog work is built after milestone work by default. Workflow dispatch (01M6VY7G), which this change set depends on, serves milestone-25 (01M6HKVRE1B7, the backlog milestone). / Where does a repo declare its [[schedules]]? The intent says 'a repo's rhiza.toml', but rhiza.toml is the root's machine-wide config (internal/rootcfg). It isn't committed in any repo and is shared by several projects. Workflow dispatch moved its rules to a committed .rhiza/dispatch.toml for the same reason, and calls a schedule another trigger kind. / Where does a scheduled run work, given every run today is on a change set and its worktree (run start <cs>)? A schedule such as Nebari's 15-minute issue intake has no change set, and opening one per firing would flood the model with draft change sets. / How do scheduled runs fit the daemon's existing limits, and what can a schedule override? The intent's defaults: after downtime a schedule runs once, and a slot is skipped while the previous run is still going.
